In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for NEF's with QVF's, the parameterization that is closest to normality in the posterior distribution is the canonical parameterization.
the canonical parameterization of a NEF-QVF model should be used for the likelihood and the canonical parameterization for the posterior distribution if a conjugate prior is used.
, in general, the parameterization of the NEF's with QVF's that is closest to the normality criterion is also closest to the tail criterion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the parameterization of a NEF-QVF that is nearest to normality in the posterior distribution is the parameterization that minimizes the variance function.
the parameterization of the NEF model that minimizes the standardized third derivative of its log-likelihood is not necessarily the one that minimizes the magnitude of the tails of the likelihood.
, for a given sample size, the best parameterization for a NEF-QVF is that which maximizes the nearness to a normal distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parameterizations for the NEF-QVFs with a conjugate inverse-Gamma prior are not as near to normality as are the parameterizations for NEF-QVFS with a conjugate gamma prior.
the parameterization of a NEF-QVF model that is closest to normal is not necessarily the best parameterization for statistical purposes.
the lognormal parameterization is the best choice for NEF-QVF's in terms of nearness to normal.
